answers.text: For the driver texts I'd just say to the AI: summarise it in three lines, keep it consistent every time, and don't leave anything important out.
I'd tell the AI to list each call as time, customer name and what it was about, in that order, so the list looks the same every time someone puts one together.
Something about the timing feels a bit rushed to me, six hours with just four people on site seems tight for a job like this. I'm not sure if that's realistic to plan for.
I had a quick look at the on-time side and the 9-late-out-of-118 math checks out fine at 92%. Something about the other number felt a bit off to me but I didn't get time to properly dig into it.
I'd go with Output 2, it just has more information in it which feels more thorough to me for a report.
I'd probably just send Email 1, it sounds more direct and to the point for opening a negotiation like this.

1. Vendor's pricing — not sure, probably better to check first. 2. Total procurement spend, aggregate — should be fine. 3. Unsigned draft of next year's budget — no, that's not something to paste anywhere yet. 4. Datasheet from the vendor's own website — I'd still be careful with it even though it's public, better safe. 5. Employee's home address — no, that's personal, keep that well away from any tool like this.
I'd just ask the client directly if it's okay to summarise their agreement with an AI tool before doing anything with it.
I'd give the monthly summary a read-through before it goes out, just to make sure it looks right.
I think step one is important, if the AI misreads the invoice numbers from the PDF then everything built after that is wrong too.
